disposition_reason: Targeted outbreak testing: Table 1 prints lead and chromium for recalled apple cinnamon puree pouches and the adulterated ground cinnamon; retail surveillance gives a range for high cinnamon samples.

study.design: Outbreak investigation (traceback, epidemiology, targeted product testing) and post-incident retail cinnamon surveillance
study.origin: Fruit puree pouches made by one manufacturer in Ecuador; ground cinnamon processed in Ecuador
study.market: US retail and homes (North Carolina, Maryland, Pennsylvania, Virginia); FDA samples at the manufacturer
study.period_text: Investigation October 2023 to 2024; pouches distributed November 22, 2022 to October 26, 2023; retail cinnamon surveillance December 2023 to June 2024
study.method: FDA multi-laboratory validated ICP-MS method for lead and chromium; Raman microspectroscopy for lead chromate; one state used a US EPA lead method
study.qa: FDA reviewed state analytical packages; validated multi-laboratory method

controls.control: Cinnamon ingredient vs cinnamon-free products from the same manufacturer
controls.comparator: Manufacturer A products without cinnamon and cinnamon products from other manufacturers
controls.outcome: Non-cinnamon products and other manufacturers' products had no actionable lead; apple cinnamon pouches 1.44-6.43 ppm Pb

controls.control: Intact cinnamon sticks vs ground cinnamon from the grinding processor
controls.outcome: Intact sticks sampled by Ecuadorian authorities were free of lead; contamination attributed to lead chromate added during or after grinding

regulatory_or_exposure.what: FDA action level for lead in processed fruits for infants and young children under 2 (guidance)

unresolved: Table 1 NCDHHS rows (1.9, 1.9, 2.3, 2.5, 2.9, 3.0, 3.1, 5.2, 5.2 ppm) are North Carolina results already reported in Napier et al. 2024 MMWR (napier2024-wanabana-lead-apple-cinnamon) and LeBlanc et al. 2024 (the introduction cites 1.9-5.2 mg/kg); not re-extracted as new data
Text gives puree chromium 0.59-1.41 ppm, but Table 1 Maryland rows print 1.53, 1.57 and 1.71 ppm
Table 1 lists the cinnamon firm as Distributor E while the text says the batches were collected from Manufacturer A; both recorded in group text
Lead chromate concentration in the puree was below the Raman method detection limit
Packaging materials were below LOD for lead and chromium (not a food finding)
Targeted outbreak data: never use as background occurrence for fruit purees
